title_en: Vying with One Another in Good Works
body_ar: جعل الله هذه الدار دار ابتلاء وامتحان، وجعل الآخرة دار جزاء وثواب، وأمرنا في هذه الدار بالمبادرة إلى الطاعات والمسابقة إلى الخيرات، وأن نستغل أعمارنا بما يرضي الله سبحانه وتعالى حتى نثقل موازيننا بالأعمال الصالحة، وحذرنا سبحانه وتعالى من الشيطان ومشاغله ومكائده، فهو عدو لدود للمؤمنين، وأمرنا باتخاذه عدواً. ضرورة المبادرة إلى الطاعات واغتنام الأوقات: بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم الحمد لله رب العالمين، وأصلي وأسلم على من بعث رحمةً للعالمين، وعلى آله وأصحابه، ومن اهتدى بهديه واستن بسنته إلى يوم الدين. أما بعد: فإن الوقت هو الحياة، وإن عمر الإنسان قصير، وإن هذه الحياة هي دار الامتحان، فعلى الإنسان أن يبادر فيها للطاعات ما دامت الفرصة مواتية وسانحة، فإن هذه الدنيا دار انتقال، وبقاء الحال من المحال، ولذلك سرعان ما ينتقل عنها الإنسان ولم يشف منها غله، بل إن الذين انتقلوا من هذه الدار يتمنون الرجوع إليها ولو لحظة واحدة ..
body_en:
*[Site synopsis]* God has made this abode an abode of trial and testing, and has made the hereafter an abode of recompense and reward. He has commanded us, in this abode, to hasten to acts of obedience and to vie with one another in good works, and to use our lifetimes in what pleases God, glorified and exalted is He, so that we may make our scales heavy with righteous deeds. And He has warned us, glorified and exalted is He, against Satan and his preoccupations and his stratagems, for he is a bitter enemy to the believers, and He has commanded us to take him as an enemy.

## The necessity of hastening to acts of obedience and of seizing the moments

In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Mercy-Giving. Praise belongs to God, Lord of the worlds. I ask God's blessing and peace upon the one sent as a mercy to the worlds, and upon his family and his Companions, and upon all who have taken guidance from his guidance and followed his practice until the Day of Judgement. To proceed:

Time is life; a person's lifetime is short; and this life is the abode of testing. So a person must hasten within it to acts of obedience, while the opportunity is favourable and open, for this world is an abode of passage, and for a state to remain unchanged is impossible. Therefore a person passes on from it quickly, without having slaked his thirst for it; indeed those who have passed on from this abode wish to return to it even for a single moment ..

flags.note: IMPORTANT. Record 669 in this same slice carries exactly this title and nothing else — it is a title-only stub with no body at all, of the kind the corpus inventory counts as audio-only. This record carries the same title with a synopsis and the opening of a written lesson. The two are very probably the same lesson entered twice, once as a bare title and once with text; they are dated four months apart in the CMS, which proves nothing given that the timestamps are upload dates. They have NOT been merged — style guide section 11 forbids deduplicating unilaterally — but the site must not present them as two separate lessons, and 669 should not be published as a bare stub if this record is its text.

The first paragraph is a synopsis written by the site — it speaks about the lesson and its subject in the third person and does not begin with the opening formula. Everything from the section heading onward is transcribed speech in the Sheikh's own voice, opening with the basmalah and the customary blessing. The site must not present the synopsis as his words.

permanence of condition is an impossibility
flags.note: A fixed Arabic saying whose force is partly in the rhyme between al-ḥāl and al-muḥāl, which cannot be carried into English. Rendered for sense; a reviewer may prefer a more proverbial English phrasing, but it should not be replaced by an English proverb that carries a different thought.

translator_notes: One of a run of thirteen records, IDs 688-700, all uploaded on 5 and 8-9 May 2011 within a few hours of one another, all built to the same template and all excerpts. Each carries a site-written synopsis, then a section heading, then the opening formula and first lines of a lesson, and then breaks off; the full text sits behind a .doc download in the /medias/doc/c-a-* series. The uniform timestamps are a bulk upload and say nothing about when the lessons were delivered.

The record contains two distinct voices and the English keeps them apart. The opening paragraph is a synopsis written by the site, about the lesson and in the third person; everything from the section heading onward is the Sheikh's own words as transcribed. Nothing in the synopsis may be quoted as his.

The title is a Qur'anic idiom (compare 'so vie with one another in good works', Sūrat al-Baqarah 2:148) and the English keeps that register; the same rendering has been used for record 669 so that the two can be matched.
No ruling term appears anywhere in the record.
